RBA committed to further rate hikes despite deteriorating labour market, testing credibility and inflation control
AUD 'pulverised' by US economic boom, widening USD/AUD gap and pressuring import-dependent sectors
Trump diesel export ban poses direct threat to Australian energy supply and fuel costs

sectors.trend: Exploration activity robust across copper, gold, and rare earths; Rio2 Peruvian copper drill, Auric Munda high-grade gold, Sarytogan 452m copper intercept, Forrestania 210k oz gold resource, Lindian rare earths nearing production. Chinese property recovery question adds uncertainty for iron ore demand.
sectors.implications: Exploration-stage names (Aureka, Manhattan, Vista Gold) offer speculative upside; major miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) face mixed signals from Chinese demand. Rare earths (Lindian) benefit from supply-chain diversification themes.

sectors.trend: RBA hiking cycle continues despite 5-year high unemployment, creating credit stress risk. Bond yield spike pressures bank NIMs. Intergenerational Report flags fiscal deterioration. Property cooling threatens mortgage book quality.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin compression from rate volatility and rising NPL risk in property. Defensive dividend yields attractive but capital at risk if unemployment worsens.

sectors.trend: Data centre boom straining grid capacity; Trump diesel export ban threatens fuel supply; energy cost political controversy; nuclear energy debate intensifying. Fuel price fears as global buffers dry up.
sectors.implications: Energy names (WDS.AX, SXG.AX) benefit from demand but face regulatory and supply risk. Power generators face cost pass-through pressure. Nuclear policy shift could create long-term structural opportunity.

sectors.trend: Jetstar industrial action escalates; over half of renters financially stressed; Chinese EV battery innovation (5-min charge) pressures local auto; McDonald's grappling with Ozempic demand shift.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces margin pressure from Jetstar (JST) industrial action. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) see mixed demand. EV disruption threatens traditional auto supply chains.

sectors.trend: Global AI chip race intensifying (Nvidia, AMD, Intel, SK Hynix); Salesforce product launch; AI optics trade splitting. Limited direct ASX exposure but indirect via data centre energy demand.
sectors.implications: ASX tech exposure limited; primary impact via energy demand (data centres) and AUD weakness affecting tech import costs.

sectors.trend: Rising listings, falling demand driving prices lower; renter financial stress at 50%+; property market in structural correction phase.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICOL.AX) face occupancy and yield pressure. Residential property sector under stress; construction names (WBC.AX exposure) cautious.

AUD/USD divergence: US strength crushing AUD, raising import costs

Fiscal sustainability: Intergenerational Report 2026 flags tax reform urgency
Property correction: structural oversupply meeting weak demand
Industrial action: Jetstar fee waivers signal broader wage-cost pressure

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight defensive equities (CSL.AX, WES.AX); reduce leverage; hedge bond duration risk

risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor fuel supply chains; favour domestic energy producers; avoid transport-heavy exposure

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Property market correction and renter stress
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce REIT and construction exposure; monitor NPL trends in bank books

risk_assessment.mitigation: Shorten bond duration; favour floating-rate instruments; monitor 10yr GSB yields

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and copper exploration names amid strong exploration pipeline
opportunities.rationale: Auric Munda, Sarytogan 452m copper, Forrestania 210k oz, Manhattan Jaws corridor signal robust discovery pipeline; gold hedges stagflation and AUD weakness

opportunities.recommendation: Favour export-oriented major miners for AUD hedge
opportunities.rationale: AUD 'pulverised' by USD strength; BHP and RioTinto revenue in USD provides natural hedge; Chinese property recovery question adds optionality

opportunities.recommendation: Position for nuclear energy policy shift
opportunities.rationale: Nuclear ban debate intensifying; data centre energy demand structural; long-term policy change could create new ASX-listed nuclear infrastructure plays
Malawian rare earths nearing production; supply-chain diversification from China; strategic mineral policy tailwind

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce bank and REIT exposure; shift to healthcare and consumer staples
defensive_moves.rationale: Rising unemployment, property correction, and rate volatility threaten credit quality and occupancy; CSL and WES offer defensive cash flows

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD/USD exposure; avoid import-heavy consumer names
defensive_moves.rationale: AUD weakness raises input costs for retailers and manufacturers; export earners benefit

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid Qantas Group near-term; monitor Jetstar industrial action
defensive_moves.rationale: Escalating industrial action with fee waivers compresses margins; wage settlement uncertainty

defensive_moves.recommendation: Shorten bond duration; favour quality credit over long-duration government bonds
defensive_moves.rationale: Bond yield spike and RBA hiking cycle create mark-to-market losses on long bonds; 'will bonds crash stocks' risk elevated

market_outlook.short_term: ASX under pressure from RBA rate hikes, 5-year high unemployment, AUD weakness, and bond yield spike. Stagflation narrative dominates. Expect continued volatility in ^AXJO with financials and property underperforming. Miners resilient on AUD weakness. Jetstar action adds transport sector risk. 1–3 month outlook: cautious, range-bound with downside bias.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook hinges on RBA policy pivot timing, Chinese property recovery, and energy transition policy. Mining exploration pipeline (copper, gold, rare earths) supports medium-term materials sector. Intergenerational Report tax reform could create fiscal headwinds. Nuclear energy policy shift and data centre demand offer structural growth vectors. Property correction likely to continue. AUD may stabilise if US growth moderates.
